decisive_items: numerous dermal ectatic blood vessels and lymphatics with a sparse lymphocytic infiltrate
non-erythematous, non-pitting edema of the left periorbital region
8-month history of persistent swelling around his left eye
response.rationale: Biopsy showing ectatic vessels and lymphatics with sparse lymphocytic infiltrate is pathognomonic for lymphangioma; chronic unilateral periorbital edema without inflammation fits. Kimura disease typically has eosinophilic infiltrate and often systemic features, not supported here.

rejected.why: Lymphoma would show atypical lymphoid infiltrate, not ectatic lymphatics.
Pseudotumor usually has inflammatory infiltrate and responds to steroids; biopsy contradicts.
ALHE requires eosinophilia and vascular proliferation with histiocytoid endothelial cells, not described.
Sarcoidosis would show non-caseating granulomas, absent.
Angioedema is transient and lacks lymphatic ectasia on biopsy.
Orbital lymphoma would show atypical lymphocytes, not ectatic lymphatics.
Kimura disease has eosinophilic abscesses and elevated IgE; not present.
Blepharochalasis is recurrent eyelid edema with dermal atrophy, not lymphatic ectasia.
Sjögren's involves dry eyes/mouth and autoimmune features, absent.
